evidence.text:
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *ŋʷaːds): semantic 卜 + phonetic 月 (OC *ŋod).
According to 学研漢和大字典 (Gakken Kanwa Dai Jiten), it is also an ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意); 月 originally represents a crescent moon (i.e. the moon with part “missing” to the observer). The character is thus interpreted as representing divination based on the partial phase of the moon, implying the remaining visible part of the moon is the moon's ‘outside’.
In oracle bone script, 外 was written identical to 卜, but they were distinguished by the fact that 卜 has a horizontal bar extending to the inside of the tortoise shell, while 外 has a horizontal bar extending to the outside.
evidence.kind: imported_excerpt

evidence.text: The database reports that 外’s original sense is “outside.” It presents one analysis in which the oracle-bone form uses 卜 to distinguish inside from outside by the orientation of the crack, and Western Zhou bronze forms add 月 as a phonetic marker. It records early bronze forms with 月 and later forms with 夕, noting that the two graphs were originally alike. Its cited bronze examples use 外 for “outside,” including 毛公鼎’s 內外; it also reports later “beyond / after” and kinship uses.
evidence.kind: character-specific paleographic and inscriptional account
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 外

evidence.source: 金真姬,《常用漢字二百字探源》
evidence.text: This paleographic survey illustrates Shang, Western Zhou, Spring and Autumn, Warring States, seal, and clerical forms, identifying cited Shang examples as 甲骨文合集 35570 and 35545, and later bronze examples including 靜簋、毛公鼎、外弔鼎、外卒鐸、南疆鉦. It describes the early 外 graph as rare and used chiefly in compounds for 外壬 and 外丙; Western Zhou forms show 卜 with 夕 or 月. It endorses an “outside” interpretation associated with crack orientation, citing 張玉春, while the evidence shown does not make the disputed analysis certain.
evidence.kind: scholarly paleographic survey drawing on cited inscriptions
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.field: 甲骨文 / 夕 and 月
evidence.text: The database says 夕 and 月 were originally represented by the same moon-shaped graph, later differentiated by whether an interior dot was written. It cites oracle-bone and bronze examples for evening and moon/month senses. This supports caution about describing the later 外 component as specifically “night-time 夕” when accounting for earlier shapes.

evidence.field: 形義通解; 字形; inscriptional uses
evidence.text: The entry states that 外’s basic sense is “outside.” It analyzes oracle-bone 外 as 卜, with the direction of the crack used to distinguish inside from outside; Western Zhou bronze forms add 月 as a phonetic marker, placed on the side of 卜 without the branch. It reports 外丙 and 外壬 in oracle inscriptions written with 卜. It says 月 and 夕 were originally the same graph, that early bronze 外 uses 月 and later bronze forms use 夕, and that small seal retains 夕. Bronze examples use 外 for “outside” opposite 內 (毛公鼎), “beyond/after” (南疆鉦), a daughter’s son (□孫鐘), and as a surname (外弔鼎). These are source-reported analyses and examples; the entry does not establish a full dated chronology for all senses.
evidence.kind: character-specific paleographic and inscriptional account
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 外

No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.

gaps: The earliest Shang graph’s interpretation remains disputed: one account takes it as 卜 used for “outside” by crack orientation; another interpretation treats it as an initial graph that acquired 月 as a phonetic in Western Zhou. Available inspected material does not resolve the dispute conclusively.
No original inscription image was visually inspected in this research. Shang and bronze witnesses are reported through paleographic databases and a survey’s labeled examples.

The phonetic role of 月 is reported by a specialist character database and secondary reconstruction compilations, but the exact local Baxter–Sagart 月 row was not available among supplied rows. The supplied local 外 row differs from the secondary Wiktionary transcription; avoid merging the notations.

External official Unihan character-specific page for 外 could not be retrieved despite direct requests. The local Unihan row supports current Mandarin wài, but is not emitted as external evidence. Component readings for 卜 and 月 were not checked against exact local rows.

The sources inspected document early bronze 外 for ‘outside’ and later extensions such as ‘beyond/after’ and grandson, but do not establish a complete dated chronology for foreign or Japanese uses, nor demonstrate the semantic links among all later senses.
A claim that 外 was borrowed as a whole graph to write another word was not supported by the inspected evidence. The graph’s phonetic-component question is kept separate from whole-graph borrowing.
No reuse/license assessment established permission or editorial value for a tracked extract; no extract recommendation is made.

The initial Shang form’s interpretation as 卜 encoding “outside” by crack orientation is a source-reported analysis, but the supplied materials also report other interpretations; this research did not resolve the disagreement independently from inscription images.

CUHK reports the phonetic role of 月 in bronze 外, but this research did not independently establish the source word’s precise ancient pronunciation or demonstrate a complete sound-change path. Do not treat modern readings as proof of the phonetic analysis.

The supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows are 外 MC ngwajH, OC *[ŋ]ʷˤa[t]-s and 月 MC ngjwot, OC *[ŋ]ʷat. These local rows are a same-system comparison, not external evidence; the dossier notes that a secondary transcription for 外 differs. Keep notation systems distinct.

Official Unihan direct lookups for both 外 and 月 were inaccessible. The local kMandarin rows report wài and yuè, but the required official character-specific click-through records could not be verified.

The inspected source reports inscriptional uses for outside, beyond/after, a grandson, and a surname, but does not provide a complete dated chronology or establish semantic links for “foreign” and other later senses. Do not infer chronology from a modern gloss list.

The Commons oracle-style glyph is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image. Its original image URL was verified from the description page, but image retrieval failed in this session; no visual inspection is claimed.
The secondary Commons seal-file candidate could not be inspected, so it is not selected. No reuse terms were checked for recurring source text; no tracked text extract is recommended.

The interpretation of the earliest Shang form remains disputed. CUHK reports an analysis in which crack orientation distinguishes inside and outside and 月 is added as a phonetic marker in bronze forms; the inspected evidence does not independently settle that explanation from artifact images.

The CUHK entry identifies 月 as a phonetic element but the research did not independently establish the ancient spoken source word’s precise pronunciation or a complete sound-change path. Similar Baxter–Sagart reconstructions are supporting comparison, not proof of the phonetic role.

The exact local Baxter–Sagart readings are preserved above. The dossier’s secondary transcription for 外 differs from the local table; this discrepancy remains explicit and the systems are not harmonized.

Official character-specific Unihan pages for 外 and 月 were inaccessible. Their provided local kMandarin readings are wài and yuè; neither is verified here through an upstream character record, and modern readings do not prove an ancient sound relation.

The inspected account reports bronze uses for outside, beyond/after, daughter’s son, and a surname, but gives no full dated semantic chronology or demonstrated links among these meanings. The date and development of “foreign” remain unresolved.
The supplied evidence does not support a whole-graph phonetic-loan claim for 外. This question is distinct from the proposed 月 sound component.

They are not selected as evidence for 外’s historical shapes. The 卜 file page notes permission tied to a source agreement as well as a public-domain representation statement; no extract or reuse recommendation is made.

items.selection_reason: It illustrates the oracle-bone style discussed for 外, while the disputed crack-orientation interpretation gives relevant context without treating the redraw as an artifact.
items.rights: The Commons page states CC0 1.0 and public-domain dedication for the image.

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image or a specific dated Shang witness. The earliest graph’s interpretation remains disputed.
